title: Verdict resolver spec
description: Declarative per-gate verdict-resolution spec. Replaces the hand-rolled if-chains in each sub-skill's _verdict() with an ordered, PR-reviewable precedence ladder over the set of FIRED rule IDs. A single shared interpreter (claude-oncology-skills _skills_common/resolver.py) evaluates it; both engines (target-profile, compose-dashboard) call the same interpreter, so the two engines cannot drift. GUARDRAIL (deliberately NOT Turing-complete): a resolver may ONLY pattern-match over the set of fired rule IDs — ordered precedence + when_fired / when_any_fired / when_all_fired. NO arithmetic, thresholds, loops, or data lookups: that logic belongs in a CARD (compute the label) or a METHOD (compute the number), never here. This keeps the interpreter small, typed, and unit-tested, and keeps the framework's hardest-won biology precedence (e.g. 'CRISPR beats RNAi', 'suppressor before veto') visible and reviewable instead of buried in per-skill Python.

gate.description: The sub-skill / gate this resolver governs (matches the SUB_SKILLS short, e.g. 'dependency', 'expression', 'surface_modality').

version.description: SemVer of THIS resolver spec. A verdict-precedence change is a reviewable contract bump, not a silent code diff.

clamp_verdicts.description: OPTIONAL. Verdicts a sub-skill's POST-RESOLVER Python clamp can mint that this ladder's rungs never emit (e.g. selectivity's normal-breadth / stromal-confound veto in _skills_common/selectivity_veto.py downgrades a selective axis-A verdict AFTER resolution). Declared here so the resolver lists the COMPLETE emitted enum and the emitted-set tooling (validate_verdict_tokens.py, test_kill_capable_completeness) folds them in — otherwise a nomination-gate entry for a clamp verdict is wrongly rejected as 'never emitted'. Kept in lockstep with the skill's clamp constant by a skills-side guard test.

post_resolver_clamp.description: OPTIONAL. DECLARATION (not executed by this interpreter) of the sub-skill's POST-RESOLVER Python clamp — the ONE place decision logic legitimately lives outside the rung ladder, because the clamp is conditioned on the resolver's OUTPUT verdict (it only downgrades an already-selective axis-A call), which a rung firing on the fired-set alone cannot express. Declared here so the clamp's rule_id -> verdict mapping and precedence are PR-reviewable in the contract with the SAME legibility the rungs have, closing the 'one hole in the declarative decision spine' (framework-architecture assessment, finding 6). The executor (e.g. skills/_skills_common/selectivity_veto.py) is kept in lockstep with this block by a skills-side guard test; every clamp verdict here must also appear in `clamp_verdicts`.

module.description: Repo-relative path of the Python executor that applies this clamp (for traceability).

direction.description: One-directional guarantee. `downgrade_only`: the clamp can only make a selective axis-A verdict MORE conservative, never upgrade; it is a NO-OP on any input verdict not in `applies_to_input_verdicts`.

applies_to_input_verdicts.description: The resolver-output verdicts the downgrade may act on (the guard). A fired veto rule is a NO-OP unless the current verdict is one of these — which is exactly why this cannot be a rung.

precedence.description: ORDERED veto arms — first arm whose `when_fired` rule is in the fired set wins the clamp verdict + driving label (worst-case conjunction with explicit precedence). Every `verdict` here MUST also be listed in `clamp_verdicts`.

when_fired.description: The veto rule_id whose firing triggers this arm.

verdict.description: The clamp verdict this arm mints (also in clamp_verdicts).

upgrade.description: OPTIONAL companion one-directional UPGRADE clamp, applied BEFORE the downgrade precedence (so the downgrade arms can still act on the upgraded verdict). Lifts a rescue-eligible input verdict to `verdict` iff EVERY requirement group has >=1 fired member.

requires.description: Conjunction of groups; each inner group is satisfied by ANY of its fired rule_ids (AND-of-ORs).

modality_conditional.description: OPTIONAL. Declares that the `precedence` walk is MODULATED by the caller's optional modality lens: an arm whose OWN interpretation-rules `signals:` block declares a non-opposing signal for the chosen modality is SUPPRESSED and the walk falls through to the next arm. The signal is read from the fired rule, never from a table in the executor, so adding an arm needs no code change. Present only where a clamp is genuinely modality-conditional; absent means the clamp is modality-blind (worst-case for every modality).

signal_source.description: Where the per-modality declaration is read from. Only the fired rule's own `signals:` block is permitted — a modality table inside the executor would be undeclared logic, which is what this block exists to prevent.

suppressing_signals.description: The signal tokens that count as an EXPLICIT non-opposing declaration and therefore waive the arm. Any token NOT listed here (including a missing/unknown signal) leaves the arm in force — fail-closed. `insufficient` must NOT be listed: it is a coverage token, and a veto arm only fires when the measurement exists, so admitting it would read data availability as a safety judgement.

suppressible_verdicts.description: The clamp verdicts a modality lens may waive — normally only the KILLs. Every entry must appear in `clamp_verdicts`.

never_suppressed_verdicts.description: OPTIONAL explicit complement: clamp verdicts NO lens may waive. Use for selectivity-PRESERVING outcomes, where suppression would DELETE a named liability from the record rather than unblock a nomination.

expected_inert_arms.description: OPTIONAL. Arms that are inert BY DESIGN: the arm mints a verdict listed in `suppressible_verdicts`, but the arm's own rule is `opposing` for every modality, so no lens can ever waive it. This happens legitimately when one verdict is minted by SEVERAL arms with opposite lens behaviour — suppressibility is declared per-VERDICT and evaluated per-ARM. Declaring the arm here waives validate_resolvers' MODALITY_LENS_INERT_ARM warning for that arm ONLY, and the declaration is itself checked: it must name a real precedence arm minting a suppressible verdict, and if the arm later BECOMES waivable the declaration is a STALE_EXPECTED_INERT_ARM error, because it would then document the opposite of the safety behaviour. It can never waive VACUOUS_MODALITY_LENS — if no arm at all is reachable the whole block is still an error.

rule_id.description: The `when_fired` rule_id of the precedence arm that is inert by design.

reason.description: WHY no modality can waive this arm, in mechanism terms — not 'by design'. The reason is the reviewable part: an unexplained entry is a silencer.

requires_essential_window_class.description: OPTIONAL PRECONDITION gating every suppression on a card field rather than on the fired set — e.g. modality tolerance of broad-LOW normal expression holds only when the target is CLEAN against the essential-organ set, so a merely narrow essential window must still KILL. Read from the named card's summary; anything outside `one_of` (including a missing card or field) FAILS CLOSED.

card_id.description: The card whose summary carries the precondition field.

field.description: The summary field name to read.

one_of.description: The ONLY field values that permit suppression.

on_suppression.description: What a suppressed arm does. `fall_through_to_next_arm`: the walk continues, so a lower-precedence arm that is `opposing` for the chosen modality still takes the verdict. NOT 'the resolver verdict stands'.

no_modality_behavior.description: The guarantee when no modality lens is supplied: the walk reproduces the modality-blind precedence byte-for-byte, so every default and composed path is unaffected.

provenance_fields.description: Headline/decision fields the executor MUST emit so a waived arm is VISIBLE rather than silently absent.

resolve.description: ORDERED precedence ladder — first matching rung wins (the precedence, now visible). Each rung fires a verdict when its fired-set predicate matches.

verdict.description: The verdict string this rung emits when it matches.

when_fired.description: Matches iff this single rule_id is in the fired set. driving_rule_id = this rule_id.

when_any_fired.description: Matches iff ANY listed rule_id is in the fired set. driving_rule_id = the FIRST listed rule_id that fired (list order = tie-break, so it is deterministic).

when_all_fired.description: Matches iff ALL listed rule_ids are in the fired set (the compound conjunction — e.g. the paralog suppressor needs non-dependent-killer AND strong-paralog-buffering both fired). driving_rule defaults to the LAST listed rule_id unless `driving_rule` is set explicitly.

driving_rule.description: OPTIONAL explicit driving_rule_id for the rung (must be one of the rung's own rule_ids). Used mainly with when_all_fired to name WHICH of the conjoined rules is the provenance anchor. Defaults: when_fired → its rule; when_any_fired → first-fired; when_all_fired → last listed.

priority.description: OPTIONAL explicit precedence (0 = highest), used only when the resolver's `evaluation` is `match_all_reduce` (the Fold — VERDICT_REPRESENTATION_FOLD.md). Makes precedence EXPLICIT DATA instead of positional: match-all-then-reduce evaluates every rung and returns the matching rung of MINIMUM priority, so rung ORDER no longer affects the result (R6 order-independence). Set priority = the rung's current ladder index to be byte-equivalent to first-match by construction. Ignored under the default `first_match` evaluation.

default.description: The verdict when NO rung matches (typically 'insufficient'). driving_rule_id is null for the default. Making the default EXPLICIT is what lets the exhaustiveness validator prove there is no silent fall-through.

evaluation.description: How the shared interpreter evaluates this ladder. `first_match` (DEFAULT when absent — back-compat): the earliest matching rung wins (implicit positional precedence). `match_all_reduce` (the Fold — VERDICT_REPRESENTATION_FOLD.md): evaluate ALL rungs, return the matching rung of minimum `priority` — precedence is EXPLICIT DATA and rung order is irrelevant (R6). A `match_all_reduce` resolver MUST give every rung a unique `priority`; set them to the ladder indices to remain byte-equivalent to first_match by construction.
